what: The updateTool method is accumulating multiple responsibilities and growing in size: meta field comparison, file I/O for 5 file types, validation, change tracking, warning collection, and output formatting.
why: As more fields and file types are added, this method becomes harder to maintain and test in isolation. Each file type follows the same read-validate-compare-track pattern but the logic is inlined rather than abstracted.
verify: Read the full updateTool method and count lines/responsibilities. Check whether the method length and cyclomatic complexity have crossed a threshold where extraction into helper methods would improve readability and testability.

what: The updateTool method warns when meta.json slug differs from the target tool slug, but createTool has no equivalent warning or validation when meta.json slug differs from the directory-inferred slug argument.
why: This is an API symmetry gap. During creation, if meta.json contains a different slug, it is silently ignored with no feedback.
verify: Read createTool to confirm that the slug parameter is used directly and meta.json slug (if present) is silently ignored.

what: The updateTool has a $warnings mechanism and $filesChecked diagnostics array, but createTool has neither.
why: As the push command is the single entry point for both create and update, users expect consistent feedback quality.
verify: Read createTool's output formatting and confirm it lacks warning/diagnostic mechanisms.

what: Each file type in updateTool follows an identical pattern repeated 5 times with minor validation variations.
why: The repetition makes it easy for validation rules to drift between file types.
verify: Count the repeated blocks in updateTool and assess whether a loop-based or helper-based approach would reduce code without adding unnecessary abstraction.

what: No slug format validation when creating a new tool via tool:push
why: The createTool method accepts the slug directly from user input without validating its format. Special characters in slugs (spaces, quotes, shell metacharacters) could cause issues when the slug appears in shell commands or tool instructions displayed to the AI.
verify: Check if slug validation exists elsewhere (e.g., in PocketTool model, migration constraints, or other tool commands). Test creating a tool with slug containing special characters.

what: Error messages and success output include user-controlled directory paths and slugs without sanitization
why: Multiple error messages and success outputs interpolate user-controlled values directly. While these are returned as ToolResult text (not rendered as HTML), they are displayed in AI conversation context. If a slug or directory path contains prompt-injection-style content, it could influence the AI's behavior.
verify: Check how ToolResult text is displayed to the user and AI. Determine whether tool output is treated as trusted or untrusted content in the system prompt / conversation flow.

what: Stale reference to old 'tool:create' command name in config comment (line 102)
why: The PR renames tool:create to tool:push but missed updating this comment.
verify: Check www/config/panels.php line 102 for the stale 'tool:create' reference.

what: Stale reference to old 'ToolCreate' class name in ASCII architecture diagram (line 90)
why: The PR replaced ToolCreate/ToolUpdate/ToolShow with ToolExtract/ToolPush but missed updating this diagram.

what: New ToolExtractTool and ToolPushTool classes lack the $apiExamples property that all other tool classes in the 'tools' category define
why: Every other tool class provides $apiExamples for API consumers. Note: Already accepted as ARCH-008 in docs/review-learnings.md.
verify: Check if ARCH-008 in docs/review-learnings.md adequately covers this.

what: Unnecessary local variable $isCustomDirectory (line 148) is assigned once and used once immediately after
why: The variable adds a line without improving readability. The condition `isset($input['directory'])` is already self-documenting.
verify: Confirm $isCustomDirectory is only used once at line 149.
